quickStart:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use Useyona\EInvoice\EInvoice;

$yona = new EInvoice(['api_key' => (string) getenv('YONA_API_KEY')]);
echo $yona->mode(), "\n"; // 'sandbox' for sk_test_, 'live' for sk_live_

$readiness = $yona->organization->getReadiness();
echo json_encode($readiness, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT), "\n";

recipes.title: Your first invoice
recipes.summary: Create a buyer and an item, draft an invoice, finalise it, submit it to the tax authority, follow its status and download the PDF and the QR payload.

steps.title: Create the client
steps.text: Pass only your API key. An sk_test_ key works in sandbox and an sk_live_ key in live, on the same host.

steps.title: Create a buyer
steps.text: A buyer is the party you invoice. A B2B buyer carries its tax id (TIN), which the tax authority checks on submission. A TIN is unique per organisation: on 409 RES002, reuse the buyer you already have.

steps.title: Find an HS code
steps.text: Goods carry an HS code. Search the reference list for one that fits your product.

steps.title: Create an item
steps.text: Save what you sell once and reuse it on every invoice. Amounts are integer minor units (kobo for NGN), sent as strings.

steps.title: Draft the invoice
steps.text: A draft can be edited freely. The SDK sends an Idempotency-Key, so a retried create is never charged twice.

steps.title: Finalise it
steps.text: Finalising freezes the seller and buyer onto the invoice and runs the jurisdiction's checks.

steps.title: Submit it to the tax authority
steps.text: Submission is asynchronous: the answer is the queued submission. Webhooks tell you when it settles.

steps.title: Wait for the outcome
steps.text: Poll the status as last recorded (or listen for invoice.accepted / invoice.rejected webhooks).

steps.title: Ask the tax authority directly
steps.text: queryStatus asks the authority now instead of reading the last recorded state.

steps.title: Download the PDF
steps.text: The PDF bytes come back as a string in a BinaryResponse. getDownloadLink returns a short-lived URL instead.

steps.title: Read the QR payload
steps.text: Once registered, the invoice carries the verification payload to print as its QR code.

recipes.title: Receive webhooks
recipes.summary: Verify the Yona-Signature of each delivery over the raw body, dispatch by event type, and inspect deliveries with the SDK. Endpoints are registered in the dashboard: an API key can read and test them, not create them.

steps.title: Keep the endpoint secret
steps.text: Register your endpoint URL in the dashboard (Developers, Webhooks); it shows the signing secret (whsec_…) once. Keep it in your environment.
steps.sdk:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface;
use Useyona\EInvoice\EInvoice;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\WebhookException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Webhooks;

$secret = getenv('YONA_WEBHOOK_SECRET') ?: 'whsec_local_example_secret';

steps.title: Read the raw body
steps.text: The signature covers the exact bytes Yona sent. Read the body as a string (the PSR-7 body stream, or file_get_contents('php://input') without a framework); never verify a re-serialised array.

steps.title: Dispatch by event type
steps.text: Deduplicate on $event['id']: a redelivery carries the same id. Answer 2xx quickly and do slow work afterwards.

steps.title: Verify every delivery
steps.text: Webhooks::verifyWebhook checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature and the timestamp (±300 s) and returns the parsed event. Refuse anything it rejects with 400. The handler is a PSR-15-style function: pass it the request your framework gives you.

steps.title: Test your handler locally
steps.text: Webhooks::signWebhookPayload signs a payload exactly as Yona does, so you can exercise the handler before going live, here with a PSR-7 request built in-process. A tampered body is refused.

steps.title: List your endpoints
steps.text: The key reads the endpoints registered for its organisation and mode.

steps.title: Inspect deliveries
steps.text: Every delivery and its status: delivered, retrying or failed with the reason.

steps.title: Redeliver a failed delivery
steps.text: After fixing your endpoint, ask for one more attempt.

recipes.title: Errors and safe retries
recipes.summary: Catch the SDK's typed exceptions, branch on errorCode, quote the requestId to support, honour retryAfter, and use idempotency keys so a retried write is never applied or charged twice.

steps.title: Configure retries
steps.text: The SDK retries GET, PUT and DELETE, and writes that carry an Idempotency-Key, on network errors, timeouts, 408, 429 and 5xx. Other writes are never retried for you.
steps.sdk:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use Useyona\EInvoice\EInvoice;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\ApiException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\ConnectionException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\NotFoundException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\RateLimitException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\ServerException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\TimeoutException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Exception\ValidationException;
use Useyona\EInvoice\Http\HttpClient;
use Useyona\EInvoice\RequestOptions;

$yona = new EInvoice([
    'api_key' => (string) getenv('YONA_API_KEY'),
    'timeout' => 30,
    'retry' => ['max_retries' => 3, 'base_delay' => 0.5, 'max_retry_after' => 30],
]);

steps.title: Read a validation error
steps.text: A 400 or 422 is a ValidationException. Branch on errorCode, show errors per field, and keep requestId for support.

steps.title: Handle a missing resource
steps.text: Every API error extends ApiException, so one catch can handle them all and narrow by class.

steps.title: Make a write safe to retry
steps.text: Pass your own idempotencyKey (stored with your order, for example) so a retry after a crash or a timeout returns the first result instead of creating a second invoice.

steps.title: Wait out a rate limit
steps.text: When the SDK's own retries are exhausted, a 429 or 503 carries retryAfter (seconds). Retry only what is safe: reads, or writes with an idempotency key.

steps.title: Delete the draft
steps.text: Drafts can be deleted; their number is never reused.

recipes.title: Sandbox and live
recipes.summary: The key decides the mode: an sk_test_ key works in sandbox and an sk_live_ key in live, on the same host. Going live changes only the key.

steps.title: Create the client and read its mode
steps.text: There is no host or mode to configure. The SDK reads the mode from the key prefix.

steps.title: Make your first call
steps.text: The readiness check lists what your organisation still needs before it can invoice in this mode.

steps.title: Guard against the wrong key
steps.text: Pass assert_mode so a deployment refuses to start with a key of the other mode. The error never echoes the key.

steps.title: See your sandbox allowance
steps.text: Sandbox invoices are free within an allowance; submissions go to the tax authority's sandbox, never to the live register.

steps.title: Check the tax connection
steps.text: Each mode has its own connection to the tax authority. Live needs the organisation approved for live and its live connection made in the dashboard.

steps.title: Go live
steps.text: Create a live key in the dashboard and deploy it as YONA_API_KEY in place of the test key. Nothing else in your code changes: the same calls, the same host.

$client = new EInvoice(['api_key' => (string) getenv('YONA_API_KEY')]);
echo $client->mode() === 'live' ? 'live: submissions are reported to the tax authority' : 'sandbox: deploy an sk_live_ key to go live', "\n";

recipes.summary: List the invoices other businesses issued to you, filter them, and walk every page with paginate.

steps.title: Check the tax connection
steps.text: Received invoices arrive through your connection to the tax authority; until it is connected the list is empty.

steps.title: Read the first page
steps.text: Newest first. sync tells you whether the mirror is still filling (syncing) and when it last read the tax authority.

steps.title: Filter
steps.text: Filter by seller name or TIN, payment status, issue date, amount or currency.

steps.title: Walk every page
steps.text: EInvoice::paginate fetches page after page for you. Received invoices return an object with items, so map each page to a Page of its items.

steps.title: Summarise
steps.text: Totals by status and seller for a period.

steps.title: The same for any list
steps.text: Every list method returns a Page with data and pagination, so paginate works on it directly.
